abstract: We prove HC for all powers of the very general member of new families of abelian varieties with Hodge rings not generated by divisors. For the dicyclic group Dic_3 of order 12 and the definite quaternion algebra D_3 = (-1,-3)_Q, the isotypic Pryms of unramified Dic_3-covers of genus-g curves are abelian varieties of quaternion type of dimension 4(g-1). For g >= 3, on the Hurwitz component of a phi-redundant cover, the very general one has Hodge group SO(4(g-1)) and HC in all powers; quaternionic classes are algebraic on every such Prym. For Q_8 this extends van Geemen–Verra to all genera. In genus 3 the Prym map is dominant, which gives HC for all powers of each half-spin Kuga-Satake factor of (U^2 + A_2(-1)^2)_Q at full-group points. More generally, for every definite quaternion algebra $D$ over $\mathbf Q$ with finite ramification $S$, central products of the groups $C_p\rtimes C_{2(p-1)}$ (and $Q_8$) give $D$-type Pryms of dimension $2\varphi(m)(g-1)$, $m=2\prod_{p\in S}p$. Their quaternionic classes are algebraic on every member, and for $g\ge|S|+2$ on the Hurwitz component of a $\varphi$-redundant cover HC holds for all powers at the very general one. A separately certified genus-two family of $D_5$-eightfolds has full monodromy, with HC for all powers of its whole genus-41 Jacobian. For every odd prime $p$ and $g\ge3$, HC holds for all powers of the whole Jacobian of a very general $\varphi$-redundant $C_p\rtimes C_{2(p-1)}$-cover. For every imaginary quadratic field K, the groups Z/m semidirect Gal(Q(zeta_m)/K) give families of abelian varieties of split Weil type for K, of dimension phi(m)(g-1), with Hodge group SU and HC in all powers at the very general point. Cycles come from Schoen's cyclic subcovers via the group algebra; Hodge groups from GLLM and André. Mixed Kuga-Satake classes, the Kuga-Satake correspondence and GHC remain open.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary: v4 makes the minor improvements suggested in the v3 acceptance review; no new results. (1) The abstract states g ≥ |S|+2 and the redundancy condition for the uniform-D claim, and separates the genus-two D_5 family and its genus-41 Jacobian; mathematical notation in the new sentences uses LaTeX. (2) §7.8: the evaluation map S → ⊕ M|_{p_i} is an isomorphism because its kernel is H⁰(E₀, ν) = 0, and the Lange–Ortega codifferential is restricted explicitly to the primitive pairs {k,−k}. (3) The supplement section lists the genus-41 certificates and audit; the floating-point invariant-form audit is distinguished from the exact coefficient-form check and the duality argument; the supplement README is updated. (5) NEW §7.11. For every odd prime p and g ≥ 3, HC holds for all powers of the whole Jacobian (dimension 1+2p(p−1)(g−1)) of a very general φ-redundant G_p-cover, e.g. Dic₃ (p = 3) in genus 3 gives dimension 25. This extends §7.9 (p = 5). The only Q-isomorphic blocks are A_e and A_{2e} (e odd, same cyclotomic field). A Goursat dichotomy on the semisimple Hodge group shows that either they are independent, or they are coupled by a graph, in which case they are isogenous by Lefschetz (1,1). So no joint monodromy computation is needed. Supporting scripts: Gp_character_table.py (exact characters, p ≤ 11) and whole_jacobian_Gp.py (dimensions; Goursat clashes). §7.11 also cites the general any-G theorem of rStation hodge_conjecture_40 (v1, published 22 Oct), of which it is the special case G = G_p with an independent proof that uses neither Brauer induction nor joint handlebody monodromy. (4) Milne's Class Field Theory and Voight's Quaternion Algebras are now numbered references [24], [25].

coauthors.contribution: Auxiliary cyclic cover Y = X/<a^2> -> C and the contraction isolating the Weil classes on P_D (Theorem A'); first-fundamental-theorem argument for all powers (Section 4); discriminant from the GLLM basis (Remark 8.1); genus-three nodal dominance (Theorem C), rational transport (Corollary C.1), the Kuga-Satake polarization comparison (Proposition C.2, Corollary C.3); exact verification scripts; full audits of the manuscript. Theorem E (§7): the all-definite-D construction (the groups G_D, the Brauer computation, the Morita pullback of Schoen's cyclic determinant classes) and its exact checker. Corollary §7.7 (genus-two D_5 eightfolds) and its monodromy certificate. §7.8 (period-image dimension) and §7.9 (HC for all powers of the whole G_5-Jacobian). §7.10 (genus-41 whole Jacobian) and its certificates.
